problem.concept: The increasing volume of unsolicited bulk e-mail (spam) has generated a need for reliable anti-spam filters.
anti-spam filters have so far been based mostly on keyword patterns that are constructed by hand and perform poorly.

task.concept: investigate the performance of two machine learning algorithms in the context of anti-spam filtering

contribution.concept: suitable cost-sensitive evaluation measures
Naive Bayesian filter; memory-based learning approach: Both methods achieve very accurate spam filtering, outperforming clearly the keyword-based filter of a widely used e-mail reader.

problem.concept: word embeddings are unable to model the dynamic nature of words' semantics, i.e., the property of words to correspond to potentially different meanings.
very few evaluation benchmarks exist that specifically focus on the dynamic semantics of words.

contribution.concept: WiC
existing models have surpassed the performance ceiling of the standard evaluation dataset for the purpose, i.e., Stanford Contextual Word Similarity

problem.concept: the"bag-of-words"assumption is usually made which ignores the ordering of words. This assumption simplifies the computation, but it unrealistically loses the ordering information and the semantic of words in the context.

method.concept: represent each topic as a cluster of multi-dimensional vectors and embed the corpus into a collection of vectors generated by the Gaussian mixture model

contribution.concept: GMNTM
GMNTM: our model can learn better topics and more accurate word distributions for each topic.
comparing to state-of-the-art topic modeling approaches, GMNTM obtains significantly better performance in terms of perplexity, retrieval accuracy and classification accuracy.

problem.concept: it is usually hard to determine the hyper-parameters of RBF kernel functions.

A multiple kernel learning (MKL) algorithm is developed to solve this problem, by which the kernel matrix weights and Lagrange multipliers can be simultaneously obtained with semidefinite programming. However, the amount of time and space required is very demanding.

method.concept: two stage multiple kernel learning algorithm by incorporating sequential minimal optimization (SMO) with the gradient projection method

contribution.concept: two stage multiple kernel learning algorithm by incorporating sequential minimal optimization (SMO) with the gradient projection method
two stage multiple kernel learning algorithm: Experimental results on data sets from UCI and Statlog show that the proposed approach outperforms single-kernel support vector clustering.

detecting thoughtful comments: the most useful features include the discourse relations and relevance features along with basic textual features to predict the comment quality in terms of thoughtfulness.

detecting thoughtful comments: logistic regression model: In our experiments on two different datasets, we could achieve a prediction score of 79.37% and 73.47% in terms of F-measure on the two data sets, respectively.

task.concept: detecting topic-based influencers in social media

method.concept: behavioral model of authors and readers
content-based citation graph, where nodes represent authors with their generated content and edges represent reader-to-author citations
first profile the content of authors (nodes) and citations (edges) and derive topic-based similarity scores to the topic
three different extensions of the Topic-Sensitive PageRank algorithm that exploit the similarity scores to find topic-based influencers

contribution.concept: behavioral model of authors and readers
three different extensions of the Topic-Sensitive PageRank algorithm that exploit the similarity scores to find topic-based influencers

three different extensions of the Topic-Sensitive PageRank algorithm: a large real-world dataset that was gathered from Twitter by measuring information diffusion in social networks: overall, our methods outperform several state-of-the-art methods.

the topic uniqueness aspect in user interests within social media should be considered for the influencers detection task; this is in comparison to previous works that have solely focused on detecting topic-based influencers using the combination of link structure and topic-relevance.

problem.concept: Although the questions may involve complex relations among multiple regions, few attention models can effectively encode such cross-region relations.

method.concept: model the visual attention as a multivariate distribution over a grid-structured Conditional Random Field on image regions
convert the iterative inference algorithms, Mean Field and Loopy Belief Propagation, as recurrent layers of an end-to-end neural network

contribution.concept: model the visual attention as a multivariate distribution over a grid-structured Conditional Random Field on image regions
convert the iterative inference algorithms, Mean Field and Loopy Belief Propagation, as recurrent layers of an end-to-end neural network
Visual Question Answering: the limited effective receptive field of ResNet on two datasets

model the visual attention as a multivariate distribution over a grid-structured Conditional Random Field on image regions: We empirically evaluated our model on 3 datasets, in which it surpasses the best baseline model of the newly released CLEVR dataset, and the best published model on the VQA dataset.

task.concept: automatically identify linguistic contexts which contain possible causes of emotions or emotional states from Italian newspaper articles

method.concept: interplay between relevant linguistic patterns and an incremental repository of common sense knowledge on emotional states and emotion eliciting situations

contribution.concept: EMOCause

methodology is based on the interplay between relevant linguistic patterns and an incremental repository of common sense knowledge on emotional states and emotion eliciting situations. Our approach has been evaluated with respect to manually annotated data. The results obtained so far are satisfying and support the validity of the methodology proposed.

task.concept: Given a hierarchy represented as a rooted DAG G with n weighted leaves, one selects a subtree of the transitive closure of G that minimizes the expected path cost.
Category Tree (CT), seeks a decision tree for categorical data where internal nodes are categories, edges are appropriate values for the categories, and leaves are data items.
k nearest neighbor queries on R-trees

contribution.concept: CSS
Category Tree (CT)
Promise-Pruning
Degree cost, γ, is a function of the out degree of a node. We give a sufficient condition for γ that makes CSS NP-complete. This result holds even when the leaves have equal weight.
a polynomial time solution for instances of CSS where G does not constrain the choice of subtrees and γ favors nodes with at most k links.
Even though CSS remains NP-hard for constant degree DAGs, we give an O(log(k)γ(d+1)) approximation for any G with maximum degree d, provided that γ favors nodes with at most k links.

a complete characterization of the optimal trees for two special cases: (1) linear degree cost in unconstrained graphs and uniform probability distributions, and (2) logarithmic degree cost in arbitrary DAGs and uniform probability distributions.
Decision Tree (DT): a ln n + 1-approximation for DT and show DT does not have a polynomial time approximation scheme unless P=NP.
extension to a popular depth-first 1-nearest neighbor query results in a theoretically better search
Promise-Pruning: a class of R-trees where its application reduces the search space exponentially.

method.concept: first-order Hidden Markov model (HMM) for the word alignment problem
make the alignment probabilities dependent on the differences in the alignment positions rather than on the absolute positions

contribution.concept: new model for word alignment in statistical translation
first-order Hidden Markov model (HMM) for the word alignment problem: The difference to the time alignment HMM is that there is no monotony constraint for the possible word orderings.

method.concept: probabilistic model connecting student behavior and class performance, formulating student engagement types as latent variables

contribution.concept: probabilistic model connecting student behavior and class performance, formulating student engagement types as latent variables

probabilistic model connecting student behavior and class performance, formulating student engagement types as latent variables: our model identifies course success indicators that can be used by instructors to initiate interventions and assist students.

task.concept: determine whether preferential attachment occurs during the growth of a network
extract the preferential attachment rule using time-dependent data

method.concept: examine the growth of the network as a function of a threshold energy (rather than time), where only those transition states with energies lower than the threshold energy contribute to the network

contribution.concept: self-consistent method
self-consistent method: Model networks are grown with known preferential attachment rules to test the method, which is seen to be robust.

a scale-free inherent structure network, which represents the connections between minima via transition states on a potential energy landscape. Even though this network is static, we can examine the growth of the network as a function of a threshold energy (rather than time), where only those transition states with energies lower than the threshold energy contribute to the network.For these networks we are able to detect the presence of preferential attachment, and this helps to explain the ubiquity of funnels on energy landscapes.

a scale-free inherent structure network: the scale-free degree distribution shows some differences from that of a model network grown using the obtained preferential attachment rules, implying that other factors are also important in the growth process.
